messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed p99 for /v1/generate on EU region spiked ~300ms after yesterday's routing-policy tweak. p50/p95 unchanged. anyone seen similar?
jon: yup saw it in the heatmap. small-count endpoints only. looks like the sample source switched to 'fallback-route' for some clients.
maya: interesting — dashboard shows sample count for that slice went from ~120 -> 6. p99 jump is huge though.
ali: small sample counts can make p99 noisy. but this feels systematic: the region fallback adds a proxy hop. rough path: ingress -> fallback-proxy -> gpu -> response.
sam: can we repro with synthetic? I pushed a quick canary that forces fallback for prefix "eu-small" and ran 500 requests. results: p50 ~ 60ms, p95 ~ 90ms, p99 ~ 410ms.
lisa: do we show per-hop breakdown on the console? I remember we surface transport vs service_time in the latency pane. maybe the p99 is dominated by transport time in fallback path.
maya: console slice shows service_time stable, transport_time spike. weirdly the trace samples are sparse for that cohort.
jon: this smells like sample-origin confusion in rollup. our percentile rollup takes mixed samples from different origins (ingress vs backend) and the legend labels 'endpoint' only. ops mistake.
ali: agree — when fallback-route is used we tag samples with origin=fallback-proxy, but the dashboard rollup sometimes treats fallback as the primary origin, which changes distribution.
sam: quick idea: mark low-sample cohorts (<50) with a confidence badge and show raw sample list. then engineers won't overreact to noisy p99.
lisa: +1. also add a per-origin toggle in the breakdown so we can switch to "backend only" percentile.
maya: for short term — can someone patch the tooltip to show sample_count and top origin? I'll open a tiny PR.
jon: I can add a tooltip change. PR incoming.
alI: note — we should also audit routing-policy change to avoid silent promotion of fallback to primary path. might be an autoscaling/weighting bug. opened https://go/repo/issue/452 for investigation.
deploy-bot: deployed canary dashboard change to staging at commit 3a9f2.
maya: thanks. once the tooltip is live let's monitor for ~24h before changing alerting SLOs.Also created a small prompt to reproduce in the infra lab and put steps in the issue. :thumbsup:
jon: sounds good. follow-up: let's add an interstitial note in rollout UI when fallback increases > 5% so product owners see perf impact in advance.
sam: can prototype the UI copy. short + clear, eg: "Fallback traffic increased — expect higher network latency for affected slices."
lisa: and include link to per-origin view.
maya: perfect. closing loop for now, will post any new finds in this thread.
